messages.content: The Triangle rollout is finally mostly off my desk. I need to start the Minneapolis certification trip for late April.
Sure. What do you know so far: exact dates, where in Minneapolis, and whether any session is still tentative?
Required sessions are Tuesday and Wednesday near the medical campus. They’re talking about a Monday late-afternoon hands-on lab, but it’s not confirmed yet. I’d fly out of Denver.

Then I’d avoid locking a nonrefundable plan until the lab is settled. If Monday becomes required, arriving the same afternoon only works if the lab starts late enough and the flight is nonstop. If it stays Tuesday/Wednesday only, Tuesday morning saves a hotel night but gives you almost no delay cushion.

That’s my worry. Hotel-wise, the organizer block is closest to the meeting rooms but looks pretty basic. A North Loop hotel is better reviewed and has a pool and fitness room, no hot tub listed. There’s also a cheaper airport hotel.

For a first pass, I’d rank them this way: North Loop first if the nightly rate is acceptable, because it gives you a better stay and easy rideshare access; organizer block second for pure convenience, especially if the lab runs late; airport hotel third unless you rent a car, because it makes every campus move longer.
I would rather not rent a car unless it’s clearly useful. I’ll have a backpack and maybe one small kit, not the big demo case.

Then skip the car for now. MSP to North Loop is straightforward by rideshare, and rideshares to the medical campus should be simpler than parking. I’d only add a car if the organizer confirms off-campus evening lab work or awkward multiple sites.
What flight pattern would you put in front of my director?

Three choices, ranked: 1) If the Monday lab is required and check-in is before about 5:00, fly Sunday late afternoon or evening and add one hotel night. 2) If the lab starts later, use a Monday nonstop from Denver that lands mid-to-late afternoon, but make sure there is at least 90 minutes between scheduled landing and check-in. 3) If there is no Monday lab, fly Monday afternoon or evening and be rested for Tuesday; I would not make a Tuesday morning arrival the lead plan.
Carrier doesn’t matter. I just want the cleanest route. If there’s a good nonstop in the afternoon, that’s better than saving a little with a connection.

Agreed for this trip. Denver to Minneapolis has nonstop options, so I’d keep the search to nonstop first and only price a one-stop as a fallback if fares spike. For the return, Wednesday evening is reasonable if the credential review ends by 4:00 or 4:30; otherwise Thursday morning is safer.
What do I need from the workshop people before I book?

Ask them for: whether the Monday lab is required, the exact Monday check-in and end time, the building and room near the medical campus, Tuesday start time, Wednesday credential-review release time, whether any materials need to be carried between sites, the hotel-block cutoff and cancellation terms, and whether the North Loop area is acceptable for attendee lodging. My first plan would be North Loop plus no rental car, with the flight date held open until the Monday lab decision lands.

messages.content: Minneapolis update: the Monday practical lab is required. Check-in opens at 3:15 p.m., and they said late arrivals may not be admitted.

Then I would not do the Monday same-day one-stop. Even a modest delay or bag slowdown would put you on the edge. The safer move is to fly Sunday late afternoon nonstop, settle in, and use Monday morning for email and transit to campus.
That’s what I was thinking. What did the flight options look like?

Best fit: Sunday late-afternoon DEN-MSP nonstop, landing early evening. It costs more than the Monday morning one-stop, but it protects the required lab. For the return, there is a Wednesday evening nonstop after the final credential review; Thursday morning adds another hotel night and only helps if the review runs late.
Do we know the Wednesday release time?

They put the credential review at 2:30 to 4:00, with overflow to 4:30. A 7-ish p.m. nonstop from MSP gives you time to leave campus, collect your bag if needed, and get through security without rushing.
Okay, choose Sunday late-afternoon nonstop out and Wednesday evening nonstop back. Coach is fine.
Good. I’ll set it up as a Sunday departure, Wednesday return, both nonstop, coach. I’ll select free window seats if available and skip anything that costs more than a minor fee.
Hotel decision: the block lost the king room. North Loop can hold a quiet king, pool and fitness, no hot tub. The business hotel near campus has a hot tub but reviews are weaker and the gym is tiny.

Take the North Loop quiet king. The stronger reviews and usable fitness setup matter more here than being a few minutes closer, and you already have a simple rideshare plan. We’ll note the no-hot-tub gap in the expense/travel note so nobody thinks you ignored the block for a luxury reason.
No rental car then?

No rental. Use rideshare from MSP to the hotel Sunday, rideshare to the medical campus Monday through Wednesday, and keep receipts. If the organizer later adds an off-site session, we can revisit, but with one campus it is cleaner without parking.
What should the actual booking checklist be?

Book in this order: 1) flights, because the Sunday nonstop is the risk reducer; 2) North Loop hotel for Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday nights with Wednesday checkout; 3) add the room request: quiet king, away from elevators and ice machines; 4) choose no-fee or low-fee window seats; 5) save the organizer email showing Monday lab admission rules for the expense file.
Anything else before I approve?

Two final checks: confirm the Wednesday review will not run past 4:30, and ask the hotel to confirm pool and fitness hours for a Sunday arrival. If those come back as expected, approve the Sunday nonstop, Wednesday evening return, North Loop quiet king, and no rental car.
